first_impression.reaction: Okay, the intro is short and the Key takeaways are right under it, so I didn't have to dig. The first bullet tells me what the thing is and the second gives me a checklist I can screenshot. But I typed 'wedding photo app' because I wanted to know which kinds exist, and the takeaways don't list them. I had to scroll to 'The main types of guest photo tool' to find that. No pop-up, no wall, so I stayed.

journey.quote: A wedding photo app gathers those pictures and videos in one private place, so they don't scatter across a hundred phones and group chats.
journey.reaction: Fine, that's the answer to 'what is it' in one line. The aunt and groomsmen bit before it is a little scene-setting, but it's short enough on my phone.

journey.quote: Check any option for browser uploads with no install, full resolution, video, moderation, a full download at the end, how long photos are kept and offline uploads.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. I'd screenshot this and use it to compare whatever I find on the app store.

journey.quote: A wedding photo app collects your guests' candid photos and videos in one private album, alongside your professional photographer's gallery rather than instead of it.
journey.reaction: Good, but I still don't know what my options look like. Shared album app, QR page, disposable camera thing? That's further down and it should be up here.

journey.section: The main types of guest photo tool
journey.quote: It is the simplest route for a mixed or international guest list. The trade-off is that browsing can be more basic than in a full app.
journey.reaction: This is the section I'd actually read. Each type has a trade-off in one line, which is exactly what I need. My family is half in India, so the no-install QR page sounds like my answer.

journey.section: The main types of guest photo tool
journey.quote: A dedicated app where guests join your event, upload and browse everyone else's photos.
journey.reaction: No app names anywhere. I searched 'wedding photo app' and half of me wanted a list. I get it, they're not pushing anything, and the checklist means I can judge apps myself. But I'll still have to Google again to find actual apps.

journey.quote: Older guests may find a new app a hurdle, and international guests on roaming plans may be reluctant to download anything.
journey.reaction: Exactly my worry, my grandmother is not installing anything. The heading 'Guests and downloading an app' is a bit vague though; I almost skipped it.

journey.section: Privacy, consent and who owns guest photos
journey.quote: This section is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated, nice, so it's current. But this section is long and full of Australian law on a phone screen. I'm in Singapore, I'd scroll past most of it. The welcome sign line is the only bit I'd actually use.

journey.section: Privacy, consent and who owns guest photos
journey.quote: A line on your welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before sharing anyone else's photo publicly, and we will remove any picture on request.
journey.reaction: That's practical. I'd copy that wording.

journey.quote: Not necessarily. Look for a tool that lets guests upload from the phone's browser after scanning a QR code, with nothing to install.
journey.reaction: FAQ answers are short and direct. This is the kind of thing I'd scroll straight to if I came back.

journey.quote: Ask before you commit: check that video is supported, kept in original quality and not cut short.
journey.reaction: Bit of a non-answer, but honest. It doesn't pretend all apps do video.

unanswered_questions: How much do these apps usually cost, or are there free ones? Just tell me roughly.
Which actual apps should I look at? The page never names one.
Is there a typical photo or guest limit I should watch for on cheaper plans?

turn_offs_found.why: Heading doesn't read like the question I'd ask. The FAQ already phrases it better: 'Do guests need to download an app to share wedding photos?'

turn_offs_found.quote: The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner treats photos and videos as [personal information under the Privacy Act 1988](https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/your-privacy-rights/social-media-and-online-privacy/photos-and-videos) when a person's identity is clear or could reasonably be worked out.
turn_offs_found.why: Long legal paragraphs in the middle of a how-to. Not wrong, just a lot of scrolling on a train for something I didn't search for.

would_share_with: My fiance, the 'What to look for before you choose' checklist
My maid of honour, the QR card and welcome sign tips

cta_reaction.quote: Speak with our [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-photo-app&utm_content=primary) team about planning your destination wedding.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a photo app answer, not a planner. It's not pushy and there's no pop-up, which I appreciate, but I'm not booking a concierge from a photo app search. I might tap the wedding planning apps link if I'm still on the train, because that's my next question.

top_3_changes: Put the types in the takeaways so the searcher gets the answer up top. Add a bullet after the first one. Old: "- A wedding photo app collects your guests' candid photos and videos in one private album, alongside your professional photographer's gallery rather than instead of it." New: "- A wedding photo app collects your guests' candid photos and videos in one private album, alongside your professional photographer's gallery rather than instead of it.\n- The main types are shared album apps, QR code upload pages with no install, disposable camera style apps, live slideshow displays and your photographer's own gallery."
Make the heading match the question. Old: "## Guests and downloading an app" New: "## Do guests need to download an app?"

Tell the searcher early that the guide compares types, not brands, so a missing app list feels deliberate rather than an omission. Old: "Here are the main types of tool, what to check, how to handle privacy and ownership, and how to make it work at a venue overseas, where Wi-Fi is never a given." New: "Rather than ranking apps, here are the main types of tool, what to check in any of them, how to handle privacy and ownership, and how to make it work at a venue overseas, where Wi-Fi is never a given."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft

No invented brand facts; app names, costs and limits listed as unanswered questions only
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings, add no new facts, name no apps and avoid fees, commissions, sourcing and vetting
HTML comments, image slots and fact markers treated as invisible

open_questions.question: The searcher's top unanswered question is cost and actual app names, which the brand deliberately leaves out. Is a one-line framing in the intro (change 3) enough, or should the panel accept this gap as a known limit of the post?

assumptions: Read on a phone in fast mode, Key takeaways plus the types section in full and the rest skimmed, per decision_behaviour.
Priya is planning her own wedding with family overseas; this detail is persona colour only and not a brand claim.
